title: Atonement

vibeProfile.oneLine: A girl's lie destroys three lives, and she spends a lifetime atoning.

summary: On a hot day in 1935, thirteen-year-old Briony misreads a moment between her sister and the housekeeper's son, and tells a lie that shatters three lives. As the story moves into the horror of Dunkirk and wartime London, her single childish act of imagination becomes a lifelong attempt at atonement, one the novel's own final turn quietly complicates. McEwan's most admired book is a beautifully written meditation on guilt, class and the terrible power, and unreliability, of storytelling itself.
whyReadIt: A perfectly built novel about one lie and a lifetime of trying to undo it. The final pages recast everything, gorgeously.

funFacts.text: Its closing twist about the act of writing itself is one of the most debated endings in recent fiction.
